newsitem.title: UK: World April oil supply up 300k bpd to 74.6 mln - IEA.
newsitem.headline: World April oil supply up 300k bpd to 74.6 mln - IEA.

text.p: World oil supply rose 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) in April to 74.6 million bpd, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
Most of the gain was due to a 200,000 bpd rise in OPEC production to 27.1 million bpd with Iraq showing the biggest individual gain, the IEA said in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report.
OPEC non-crude oil output, which includes natural gas liquids and other oils, reached 2.9 million bpd in April pushing total OPEC oil output to over 30 million bpd.
A modest pick up in non-OPEC supply to 44.6 million bpd in April accounted for the rest.
A rise in North Sea and Latin American production was off only partially offset by seasonal declines in Russia and North America, it said.
Output from the rest of the OECD and other developing countries are believed to have been generally slightly higher than in March.
The IEA said it made a large number of revisions to March and first quarter estimates of supply because of unexpected weather and technical problems at oilfields, mainly in the North Sea.
Total non-OPEC supply in March was 360,000 bpd lower than earlier anticipated, it said.
April exports from former Soviet Union countries fell slightly to 2.73 million bpd from a downwardly revised March level.
Black Sea exports and Druzhba pipeline exports fell by a combined 90,000 bpd but the fall was offset by higher Baltic exports and lower imports.

Looking forward, the IEA revised down by 100,000 bpd its forecast non-OPEC supply to 44.5 million bpd for the second quarter. It said expected additional delays in new field start-ups, slightly exceeded downward revisions for demand in the former Soviet Union.
